original_interpretation: Amkor offers turnkey packaging and test (wafer bump, probe, back-grind, package design, packaging, burn-in, system-level and final test, drop shipment), with customers buying one or more of these services.
evidence_found: "We provide turnkey packaging and test services including wafer bump, wafer probe, wafer back-grind, package design, packaging, burn-in, system level and final test and drop shipment services. Our customers use us for one or more of these services." (Amkor 10-K FY ended 2025-12-31, Item 1 Business)
notes: Correctly typed as reported_claim (company self-description of its service menu).

original_interpretation: Microchip licenses its SuperFlash embedded non-volatile memory technology to foundries, IDMs and design partners for licence fees and royalties, plus engineering-service fees.
evidence_found: "Our technology licensing business generates license fees and royalties associated with technology licenses for the use of our SuperFlash® embedded flash and other technologies. We also generate fees for engineering services related to these technologies. We license our Non-Volatile Memory technologies to foundries, integrated device manufacturers and design partners throughout the world" (10-K FY2025, Item 1 Business)
notes: Licensee list is stated for "Non-Volatile Memory technologies" (SuperFlash is one). Not outdated: identical wording re-checked in the Microchip FY2026 10-K (https://ir.microchip.com/sec-filings/all-sec-filings/content/0000827054-26-000016/mchp-20260331.htm).

original_interpretation: Photronics often sells under an understanding that, while its performance stays competitive, it receives a specified percentage of a customer's photomask orders, with pricing parameters negotiated per customer after qualification.
evidence_found: "Generally, Photronics and each of its customers engage in a qualification and correlation process before we become an approved supplier. Thereafter, ... we typically negotiate pricing parameters for the customer’s order. ... In many instances, we enter into sales arrangements with an understanding that, as long as our performance is competitive, we will receive a specified percentage of that customer’s photomask orders." (10-K FY2025, Item 1)
notes: "Often" paraphrases "In many instances". Company describing its own sales arrangements in a filing; fact type acceptable.

original_interpretation: Photronics states that photomask demand depends mainly on the number of new designs rather than on chip sales volumes.
evidence_found: "We believe that the demand for photomasks depends primarily on design activity rather than sales volume from products using photomask technologies. Consequently, an increase in semiconductor or FPD sales does not necessarily result in a corresponding increase in photomask sales." (10-K FY2025, Item 1A Risk Factors)
notes: Source says "design activity"; claim's "number of new designs" is a fair paraphrase (same paragraph cites "a slowdown in the introduction of new semiconductor or FPD designs"). Correctly typed reported_claim ("We believe"); applies to ICs and FPDs.

original_interpretation: Photronics sold to about 636 customers in fiscal 2025 (IDMs, fabless companies and pure-play foundries), with the top three accounting for about 16%, 13% and 8% of revenue.
evidence_found: "These include integrated device manufacturers, fabless semiconductor companies, and “pure-play” foundries. During 2025, we sold our products to approximately 636 customers. For fiscal year 2025, Customer A, B and C accounted for approximately 16%, 13% and 8%, of consolidated revenue, respectively." (10-K FY ended 2025-10-31, Item 1 Business)
notes: Fiscal year confirmed as ended 31 Oct 2025 (cover page). Customer counts include FPD as well as semiconductor customers.

original_interpretation: GlobalFoundries earns most of its revenue from finished wafers priced on a per-wafer basis for each customer design.
evidence_found: "Revenue Recognition – The Company generates the majority of revenue from volume production and sales of finished semiconductor wafers, which are priced on a per-wafer basis for the applicable design." (20-F FY2025, Summary of Material Accounting Policies, R11)

original_interpretation: Besides wafers, GlobalFoundries earns non-wafer revenue from NRE services, mask production, process qualification, post-fab bump/test/packaging services, and IP licences with royalties.
evidence_found: "We also generate non-wafer revenue from rendering non-recurring engineering (“NRE”) services, mask production, process qualification, post-fabrication services such as bump, test, and packaging, and revenue from intellectual property licenses and related royalties." (20-F FY2025, Revenue Recognition, R11)

original_interpretation: GlobalFoundries recognises wafer revenue at a point in time, when wafers ship from its fab or are delivered to the customer, while NRE services are recognised over time on a cost-incurred basis.
evidence_found: "The performance obligations are satisfied at the point in which control of the wafers is transferred to the customer, which is determined to be at the point of wafer shipment from the Company’s facilities or delivery to the customer location. NRE services are recognized over time as the Company performs the services based on a percentage of costs incurred over total expected costs." (20-F FY2025, R11)

original_interpretation: GlobalFoundries' master supply agreements can set volume-based pricing formulas, volume discounts and yield-adjustment calculations on top of purchase orders.
evidence_found: "The Company also enters into master supply agreements (“MSA”) with certain customers that may specify additional terms and conditions, such as pricing formulas based on volume, volume discounts, calculation of yield adjustments, indemnifications, transfer of title and risk of loss and payment terms." (20-F FY2025, R11)

original_interpretation: Some GlobalFoundries long-term supply agreements carry minimum volumes with a breakage fee if the customer does not meet the commitment; GF treats estimated breakage fees as variable consideration recognised with wafer revenue over the agreement term.
evidence_found: "For certain customers under long-term supply agreements (“LTAs”) with minimum volume requirements that are subject to a certain breakage fee if such commitment is not met" ... breakage fee estimated "as variable consideration and includes such fee in the contract transaction price if not constrained" ... "breakage fees that are constrained are not included in the contract transaction price" (20-F FY2025, R11)
correction: Breakage fees are included in revenue only if not constrained; the filing says LTA volumes "are usually not guaranteed and subject to subsequent negotiations or changes", and constrained breakage fees are excluded from the transaction price. The claim omits this constraint.

original_interpretation: GlobalFoundries accrues volume rebates and yield adjustments, refundable to customers by credit note, as reductions of wafer revenue.
evidence_found: "The Company estimates the variable consideration related to volume rebates and yield adjustments for certain contracts that may be refundable to customers through the issuance of a credit note ... These potential revenue adjustments are accrued and netted against accounts receivable on the consolidated statements of financial position." (20-F FY2025, R11)
notes: Applies to "certain contracts" and is subject to a constraint; accruals are netted against receivables.

original_interpretation: GlobalFoundries is typically paid 30-60 days after invoice, so it records no significant financing component on wafer sales.
evidence_found: "As a practical expedient, the Company does not adjust the amount of consideration for the effects of a significant financing component as payment is received shortly from the time the performance obligations are satisfied, which is typically between 30 and 60 days from the invoice date." (20-F FY2025, R11)

original_interpretation: GlobalFoundries recognises fixed-fee process-IP licence revenue at a point in time and related royalties when the licensee sells products using the technology.
evidence_found: "The IP licenses are “right to use” licenses ... such as patents to a specialized manufacturing process ... License revenue that is charged as a fixed fee is recognized at a point in time when the customer is provided with the right to use the license. Related royalty fees are recognized when the related sales of the product incorporating the licensed technology occur." (20-F FY2025, R11)

original_interpretation: TSMC recognises revenue when customers obtain control of goods, generally on delivery to the customer's specified location, net of estimated returns, rebates and allowances.
evidence_found: "The performance obligations are satisfied when customers obtain control of the promised goods, which is generally when the goods are delivered to the customers’ specified locations. ... Revenue is reduced for estimated customer returns, rebates and other similar allowances." (20-F FY2025, Revenue Recognition, R11)

original_interpretation: TSMC's payment terms are in principle 30 days from invoice or 15 days after the end of the invoice month.
evidence_found: "In principle, payment term granted to customers is due 30 days from the invoice date or 15 days from the end of the month of when the invoice is issued." (20-F FY2025, Revenue Recognition, R11)

original_interpretation: Wafer sales were NT$3,272.6 billion of TSMC's NT$3,809.1 billion 2025 net revenue; the remaining NT$536.5 billion was 'Others'.
notes: Rounding checked: 3,272.6 + 536.5 = 3,809.1 NT$ bn. "Others" is not itemised in the note.

original_interpretation: TSMC held NT$189.9 billion of customer 'temporary receipts' (payments to retain capacity) at end-2025, down from NT$291.1 billion at end-2024.
evidence_found: Note c. Temporary receipts (NT$ millions, Dec 31 2024 / Dec 31 2025): current "$198,602.6 | $146,559.3", noncurrent "92,499.2 | 43,298.9", total "$291,101.8 | $189,858.2"; "The Company’s temporary receipts from customer are payments made by customers to the Company to retain the Company’s capacity." (20-F FY2025, R28)
notes: Year-end balance; later quarterly balances may differ. Refund or offset against receivables is "determined by mutual consent".

original_interpretation: UMC, the second pure-play foundry sampled, recognises revenue from wafer sales and joint technology development on transfer of control, at contractual prices less returns and allowances.
evidence_found: "Revenues on the Company’s contracts with customers for the sales of wafers and joint technology development are recognized as the Company satisfies its performance obligations to customers upon transfer of control of promised goods and services. The Company recognizes revenue at transaction price that are determined using contractual prices reduced by sales returns and allowances" (UMC 20-F FY2025, Note 4, R12)
notes: Page identity confirmed as UMC (subsidiary table lists "UMC GROUP (USA)"). "Second pure-play foundry sampled" is the researcher's framing, not a source statement.

original_interpretation: Intel Foundry's segment revenue is substantially intersegment revenue from wafers, substrates and related services sold to Intel Products and other Intel businesses.
evidence_found: "Intel Foundry ▪ Segment revenue: consists substantially of intersegment product and services revenue for wafer fabrication, substrates and other related products and services sold to Intel Products and certain other Intel internal businesses." (10-K FY2025, Note 3 Operating Segments, R12)

original_interpretation: Intel records intersegment sales from Intel Foundry to its product groups at prices intended to approximate market pricing.
evidence_found: "Intersegment sales are recorded at prices that are intended to approximate market pricing." (10-K FY2025, Note 3 Operating Segments, R12)

original_interpretation: Intel Foundry recognises internal wafer revenue on transfer of ownership, generally at completion of wafer sort, and back-end service revenue at completion of assembly and test milestones.
evidence_found: "Product revenue is recognized upon transfer of ownership, which is generally at the completion of wafer sorting. Backend service revenue is recognized upon the completion of assembly and test milestones, which approximates the recognition of revenue over the service period." (10-K FY2025, Note 3, R12)

original_interpretation: Intel Foundry's third-party foundry and assembly/test revenue from external customers was US$307 million in 2025 (US$159 million in 2024, US$547 million in 2023).
evidence_found: "Intel Foundry also includes certain third-party foundry and assembly and test revenues from external customers that totaled $307 million in 2025, $159 million in 2024 and $547 million in 2023." (10-K FY2025 ended 2025-12-27, Note 3, R12)

original_interpretation: Substantially all of Intel's revenue is product sales recognised at shipment or delivery per shipping terms, with variable consideration from price concessions estimated against the transaction price.
evidence_found: "Substantially all of our revenue is derived from product sales. ... the revenue for combined performance obligations and standalone product sales is recognized at the time of product shipment from our facilities or delivery to the customer location, as determined by the agreed-upon shipping terms. ... We determine variable consideration, which consists primarily of various sales price concessions, by estimating the most likely amount" (10-K FY2025, Note 2, R11)
notes: Intel uses the most-likely-amount method for price concessions.

original_interpretation: Texas Instruments recognises revenue on sales to distributors when control transfers, and payment from distributors is not contingent on resale.
evidence_found: "We generate revenue primarily from the sale of semiconductor products, either directly to a customer or to a distributor, and recognize revenue when control is transferred. ... For sales to distributors, payment is not contingent upon resale of the products." (TI 10-K FY2025, Revenue recognition, R11)

original_interpretation: Texas Instruments recognises revenue on consignment-inventory sales only when the customer or distributor pulls product from consignment stock held at designated locations.
evidence_found: "Revenue from sales of our products that are subject to inventory consignment agreements is recognized at a point in time, when the customer or distributor pulls product from consignment inventory that we store at designated locations." (TI 10-K FY2025, R11)
notes: "Only when" is accurate: TI says it retains control until products are pulled.

original_interpretation: Microchip gives many distributors price concessions and stock-rotation rights, which it treats as variable consideration estimated with the expected-value method.
evidence_found: "As is customary in the semiconductor industry, the Company offers price concessions and stock rotation rights to many of its distributors. As these are forms of variable consideration, the Company estimates the amount of consideration to which they will be entitled using recent historical data and applying the expected value method." (10-K FY ended 2025-03-31, R9)
notes: Not outdated: same wording re-checked in the Microchip FY2026 10-K accounting-policy note (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/827054/000082705426000016/R9.htm).

original_interpretation: Under Microchip's long-term supply agreements (typically three to five years), customers pay an upfront deposit and commit to minimum purchases for assured supply; the deposit is returned if commitments are met and may be retained otherwise.
evidence_found: "Under these LTSAs, the Company receives an upfront deposit and minimum purchase commitments from the customer in exchange for assured supply over the contract period, which typically ranges from three to five years. If the customer meets the minimum purchase commitments defined in the contract, the Company returns the deposit to the customer. If not, the Company may retain all, or a portion of the deposit" (10-K FY2025, R9)
notes: Same terms ("three years to five years") in the Microchip FY2026 10-K accounting-policy note (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/827054/000082705426000016/R9.htm). LTSAs are with "certain" customers buying via distributors or direct.

original_interpretation: Microchip, an IDM, also earns technology-licence royalties (e.g. SuperFlash embedded flash) priced as licence usage multiplied by a fixed royalty rate.
evidence_found: "Revenue generated from licensees is governed by licensing agreements. ... The final transaction price is determined by multiplying the usage of the license by the royalty, which is fixed in the licensing agreement. Revenue is recognized as usage of the license occurs." (10-K FY2025, R9)
notes: The R9 note does not name SuperFlash; the SuperFlash example is supported by SRC-0101 (Item 1: "royalties associated with licenses for the use of our SuperFlash and other technologies").

original_interpretation: NVIDIA (fabless) derives revenue primarily from product sales of hardware and systems, recognised on transfer of control, with payment generally due shortly after delivery.
evidence_found: "We derive our revenue primarily from product sales including hardware and systems. ... Payment from customers, per our standard payment terms, is generally due shortly after delivery of our products. ... Revenue from product sales is recognized upon transfer of control of products to customers" (10-K FY2026 ended 2026-01-25, R10)
notes: "Fabless" is the researcher's descriptor, not stated in this note.

original_interpretation: NVIDIA reduces revenue for customer programs: rebates to resellers and market development funds (MDFs) paid to partners.
evidence_found: "Our customer programs involve rebates, which are designed to serve as sales incentives to resellers of our products in various target markets, and MDFs which represent monies paid to our partners ... We account for customer programs as a reduction to revenue" (10-K FY2026, R10)

original_interpretation: Qualcomm treats each patent licence as a single performance obligation giving ongoing access to a changing portfolio, and estimates sales-based royalties largely from licensees' preliminary reports, with actuals reported and paid the following quarter.
evidence_found: "License agreements contain a single performance obligation that represents ongoing access to a portfolio of intellectual property over the license term" ... "Our estimates of sales-based royalties are based largely on preliminary royalty estimates provided by our licensees" ... "actual amounts reported and paid by licensees, which are generally received the following quarter." (10-K FY2025, R8)

original_interpretation: Qualcomm's service revenue and system-software licence revenue were each less than 5% of total revenue in the periods presented.
evidence_found: "Revenues from providing services and licensing system software were each less than 5% of total revenues for all periods presented." (10-K FY ended 2025-09-28, R8)

original_interpretation: Qualcomm combines a fabless chip business (QCT, US$38.4 billion FY2025 revenue) with a patent-licensing business (QTL, US$5.6 billion) out of US$44.3 billion total revenue.
evidence_found: Segment table (US$ m, FY2025): "QCT: Revenues $ 38,367"; "QTL: Revenues $ 5,582"; total revenues "$ 44,284" (reportable segments 43,949 + nonreportable 192 + unallocated 143) (10-K FY ended 2025-09-28, Segment Information, R15)
notes: Rounding checked. The total also includes QSI/nonreportable and unallocated revenue, so QCT+QTL is less than the total. "Fabless" is a descriptor; the note says QCT "develops and supplies integrated circuits and system software".

original_interpretation: Arm recognises revenue for a delivered IP licence at a point in time (on delivery or start of licence term), and treats royalty buydowns or upfront minimum royalty commitments as fixed licensing revenue.
evidence_found: "Where arrangements include royalty buydowns or upfront minimum royalty commitments, the Company treats them as fixed contract consideration under licensing revenue. Revenue allocated to the IP license is recognized at a point in time upon the delivery or beginning of the license term, whichever is later." (20-F FY2026, Note 1, R10)

original_interpretation: Arm's licences that give unlimited access to a library of current and future IP over a contract period are recognised ratably over the contract term.
evidence_found: Arrangements giving "the right to access a library of current and future IPs on an unlimited basis over the contractual period" are stand-ready obligations; "The contract consideration related to these arrangements is recognized ratably over the term of the contract in line with when the control of the performance obligations is transferred." (20-F FY2026, Note 1, R10)

original_interpretation: Arm architecture licences promise future architecture version extensions over contract terms that can run from 3 to 20 years.
evidence_found: "When architecture IP is licensed, the Company promises to provide the available architecture IPs as well as all future version extensions of the architecture IP over the contract term which could range from 3 to 20 years." (20-F FY2026, Note 1, Significant Judgments, R10)

original_interpretation: Arm accrues royalties in the quarter in which its customers ship chips containing its technology, estimating them before licensees' royalty reports arrive and truing up afterwards.
evidence_found: "Accordingly, royalties are recognized on an accrual basis in the quarter in which the customer ships their products, based on the Company’s technology that it contains." ... "Adjustments to revenue are required in subsequent periods ... primarily resulting from actual amounts subsequently reported by the licensees in the period following the accrual" (20-F FY2026, Note 1, R10)
notes: True-up part supported by the adjustment sentence; estimates also use historical trends and third-party industry data.

original_interpretation: In March 2026 Arm announced it was expanding into production silicon products with the Arm AGI CPU, adding chip sales to its licence-and-royalty model.
evidence_found: "In March 2026, we announced the expansion of our compute platform into production silicon products with the Arm AGI CPU." (20-F FY2026, Note 1, Description of Business, R10)
notes: "Adding chip sales to its licence-and-royalty model" is the researcher's reading of "production silicon products"; reasonable but not the filing's words. This is an announcement, not evidence of material chip revenue in FY2026.

original_interpretation: Arm's FY2026 (to 31 March 2026) revenue of US$4,920 million was US$2,613 million royalty revenue and US$2,307 million licence and other revenue; US$1,499 million came from related parties.
evidence_found: Note 4 table (US$ m, FY ended 2026-03-31): License and Other Revenue total "$ 2,307"; Royalty Revenue total "2,613"; total "$ 4,920"; Related Parties column total "$ 1,499" (20-F FY2026, R13)
notes: 2,307 + 2,613 = 4,920 checked. Related-party split: licence 1,009, royalty 490.

original_interpretation: Of Arm's FY2026 licence and other revenue, US$1,080 million was recognised over time and US$1,227 million at a point in time (over-time revenue was only US$121 million in FY2024).
evidence_found: "(1) Includes over-time revenue of $1,080 million, $467 million and $121 million and point-in-time revenue of $1,227 million, $1,372 million and $1,310 million for the fiscal years ended March 31, 2026, 2025 and 2024, respectively." (20-F FY2026, Note 4, R13)
notes: 1,080 + 1,227 = 2,307 = licence and other revenue checked.

original_interpretation: Arm's three largest customers made up 42% of FY2026 revenue (16%, 14% and 12%).
evidence_found: "For the fiscal year ended March 31, 2026, the Company had three customers that collectively represented 42% of total revenue, with the single largest customer accounting for 16% of total revenue, the second largest customer accounting for 14% ... and the third largest customer accounting for 12% of total revenue." (20-F FY2026, Note 4, R13)

original_interpretation: Cadence's FY2025 revenue was 70% core EDA, 14% semiconductor IP and 16% system design and analysis.
evidence_found: Product category table (fiscal 2025/2024/2023): "Core EDA* 70 % | 71 % | 76 %"; "Semiconductor IP (“IP”) 14 % | 13 % | 12 %"; "System Design and Analysis 16 % | 16 % | 12 %" (Cadence 10-K FY2025, Revenue note, R11)
notes: Category allocation for remix/combination deals is estimated from expected usage (see CLM-2014).

original_interpretation: 76% of Cadence's FY2025 revenue was recognised over time and a further 4% was other recurring revenue (80% recurring); 20% was up-front, mainly hardware, individual IP licences and some software licences longer than one year.
evidence_found: Table (2025/2024/2023): "Revenue recognized over time 76 % | 80 % | 81 %", "Other recurring revenue 4 % | 3 % | 3 %", "Recurring revenue 80 % | 83 % | 84 %", "Up-front revenue 20 % | 17 % | 16 %"; "Up-front revenue is primarily generated by sales of hardware, individual IP licenses and certain software licenses with a term greater than one year." (10-K FY2025, R11)

original_interpretation: Cadence generally invoices time-based software agreements in equal quarterly amounts, although some customers pay in single or annual amounts.
evidence_found: "For Cadence’s time-based software agreements, customers are generally invoiced in equal, quarterly amounts, although some customers prefer to be invoiced in single or annual amounts." (10-K FY2025, Revenue note, R11)

original_interpretation: Some Cadence licences let customers remix among software products, and some leave product selection and user numbers to be determined later, so revenue by product category is allocated on expected usage.
evidence_found: "Certain of Cadence’s licensing arrangements allow customers the ability to remix among software products. Cadence also has arrangements with customers that include a combination of products, with the actual product selection and number of licensed users to be determined at a later date. For these arrangements, Cadence estimates the allocation of the revenue to product categories based upon the expected usage of products." (10-K FY2025, R11)
